title: Bangladesh CIRT issues critical PHP2Shell advisory
summary: National guidance urges PHP runtime patching.
description: CIRT warns that two PHP flaws can allow unauthenticated code execution in affected web deployments. Several server integrations are potentially exposed; application updates alone may leave the underlying runtime unpatched.
severityBasis: CIRT describes both vulnerabilities as Critical.
impact: Vulnerable servers may execute attacker-supplied code.
This national advisory does not establish compromise of a Bangladesh-based system.
recommendations: Install the vendor's fixed PHP runtime release and verify the version serving web requests.
Inventory containers and managed hosting; use temporary exposure controls while patching.
evidenceNote: Confirmed publication; national relevance is distinct from a confirmed local incident. No exploitation assertion is encoded here.

title: CIRT warns about destructive cloud identity abuse
summary: Compromised service principals enabled automated destructive operations.
description: CIRT summarizes a cloud intrusion involving reconnaissance, resource deletion attempts and storage-key retrieval through legitimate workload identities. The investigated case did not confirm data exfiltration or a ransom note.
severityBasis: The reviewed notice does not assign a formal severity score.
impact: Excessive identity permissions can expose cloud resources and recovery controls to destructive misuse.
recommendations: Analyst guidance: review service-principal privileges and rotate exposed credentials.
Alert on unusual key retrieval, resource deletion and backup-policy changes; protect recovery permissions separately.
evidenceNote: A national advisory about reported activity; the notice does not identify the investigated organization as Bangladeshi.

title: CIRT reviews SideCopy phishing and fileless RAT activity
summary: Malicious shortcuts abuse Windows utilities to load remote-access malware.
description: CIRT describes a campaign using deceptive archive attachments, Windows shortcut files and mshta.exe to execute malware in memory. Reported capabilities include credential theft, screen capture and remote commands.
severityBasis: No formal severity rating is assigned in the reviewed notice.
impact: Successful infection can expose credentials and files and allow remote control.
recommendations: Analyst guidance: inspect archive attachments and restrict unnecessary script-host execution.
Hunt for unusual mshta.exe network activity, persistence changes and endpoint behavior.
evidenceNote: Nationally published guidance; the source does not establish a confirmed Bangladesh victim.

title: Bangladesh government assets appear in suspected campaign targeting
summary: CIRT identifies local relevance in suspected SideWinder-associated research.
description: Recovered infrastructure reportedly contained target lists and credential-testing scripts referencing Bangladesh government systems. CIRT cautions that being listed does not prove compromise and that attribution remains uncertain.
severityBasis: CIRT calls for priority hunting but does not assign a formal severity score.
impact: Exposed applications and weak credentials can enable unauthorized access; local compromise is not established by target lists.
recommendations: Use the advisory's evidence as hunting leads and validate matches against local telemetry.
Analyst guidance: restrict administrative interfaces and remediate exposed services.
evidenceNote: Reported targeting, with explicit limits on victim confirmation and actor attribution.

title: BCSI reports coordinated cyber activity across Bangladesh sectors
summary: An August report describes disruption and unauthorized access around August 15.
description: BCSI reports defacement, data exposure and administrative or surveillance-system access affecting several Bangladeshi sectors. Its public evidence is redacted, and incomplete forensic coverage prevents confirmation of each initial-access method.
severityBasis: BCSI's Medium Sophistication assessment describes attacker capability, not incident severity.
impact: Reported disruption and exposure span multiple organization types; precise victim totals are not established here.
recommendations: Validate suspicious activity using authentication, web and host logs.
Review exposed services, credentials, privileged access and network segmentation.

timeline.title: Reported activity period
timeline.description: Incidents reportedly clustered around this date.

timeline.title: Assessment published
timeline.description: BCSI releases a qualified public account.

evidenceNote: Historical reporting; no claim that the activity remains active today.

title: CIRT warns of espionage targeting Bangladesh defence personnel
summary: A defence-themed phishing campaign selectively delivers malicious documents.
description: CIRT reports a campaign researchers attribute to DoNot Team, using a Bangladesh military-themed document and selective payload delivery. Subsequent malware supports persistence, reconnaissance and additional module downloads.
severityBasis: CIRT assesses a critical espionage risk for Bangladesh's defence and government ecosystem.
impact: Potential collection of sensitive organizational and personnel information if targeted systems are compromised.
recommendations: Analyst guidance: review suspicious Office attachments and restrict untrusted active content.
Hunt for related persistence and network indicators; assess trusted connections to defence organizations.
evidenceNote: The source supports targeted campaign reporting, not an exhaustive list of confirmed victims or current activity.

title: CIRT completes cybersecurity programme for MIST students
summary: Three-week programme covers network defence and security operations.
description: CIRT reports completion of practical training for final-year MIST computing students. Its specialists covered network security, architecture and operations, including incident response, threat analysis and vulnerability management.
severityBasis: Capacity-building news; incident severity is not applicable.
impact: Local workforce-development activity; this is not an attack or breach report.
recommendations: Read the official announcement for programme context.
Analyst guidance: consider practical incident-response exercises in staff development.
evidenceNote: Dated institutional news retained for context; it is not presented as today's activity.
